headline: Midnight Mimosa malware preinstalled on cheap Android phones, unremovable
summary: A new malware campaign, Midnight Mimosa, has been found pre-installed on budget Android devices, compromising them before they're even turned on. The malware is deeply embedded in the firmware and cannot be uninstalled.
details: Researchers have discovered a widespread malware campaign dubbed Midnight Mimosa, which is pre-installed on low-cost Android smartphones. The malicious software resides within the device's firmware, meaning it's present even before the phone is powered on for the first time.

Unlike typical Android apps, Midnight Mimosa cannot be uninstalled by the user. It operates as a persistent system app with elevated privileges, allowing it to install and remove other apps, download additional code from remote servers, and grant itself necessary permissions.

The campaign utilizes 32 disguised apps for advertising and click fraud, generating fake impressions without user consent. To evade detection, the malware can temporarily disable Google Play Protect while executing its malicious payloads, re-enabling it afterward.

Midnight Mimosa primarily targets budget Android devices built on MediaTek platforms, affecting smartphones in over 150 countries. While genuine Samsung phones are unaffected, some compromised devices are counterfeit clones of premium models.
The threat extends beyond infected phones, as 13 Google Play apps have been found communicating with the same infrastructure used by Midnight Mimosa, indicating a broader reach.

To avoid such threats, it is recommended to purchase phones from authorized sellers and invest in original devices. For those who have unknowingly acquired an infected device, replacement is the only viable solution due to the malware's unremovable nature.
